required_fixes: Replace simulated heuristic repair with actual LLM agent (real model calls, real token counting) to measure M-repair_tokens_mean, M-browser_interactions_mean, M-verification_steps_mean as real measurements not simulation parameters
Execute actual browser interactions via Playwright instead of simulated action counts

Implement real verification function that checks postconditions on actual DOM/response state rather than deterministically generated perfect-separation scores (AUROC=1.0, precision=1.0 by construction)
Measure contamination from actual system behavior rather than hardcoded 2 events in specific failing instances
Run on real nginx 1.2x reverse-proxy with production gzip/chunked encoding and real Flask backend, not simulated headers and synthetic DOM strings
Increase per-family TEST sample size (n=6 currently) to achieve adequate power for per-family cost ratio CIs; current Wilson CI half-width ~0.22 at n=12, test n=6 is exploratory only
Decouple verification threshold calibration from deterministic instance_id-based score generation to eliminate potential TRAIN/TEST leakage through the deterministic score function
validity_findings: SIMULATION_NOT_MEASUREMENT: The entire experiment is a deterministic simulation. The 'repair LLM' is a hardcoded heuristic (execute_delta_repair.py lines 355-403), not an actual language model. Token costs, browser interactions, and verification steps are generated by deterministic functions with jitter, not measured from real execution. Per producer validity_notes: 'repair LLM simulated heuristic not real model calls - true token cost and model variance not measured, browser interactions counted but not executed via Playwright.' This makes C5 (cost ratio) and C8 (amortized cost) measurements of simulation parameters, not of any real repair system.

VERIFICATION_AUROC_ARTIFACTUALLY_PERFECT: Verification scores (y_scores_test_extended) are generated deterministically from instance_id with perfect separation between success/failure classes by construction (lines 498-513 in execute_delta_repair.py). AUROC=1.0, precision=1.0, recall=1.0 are mathematical consequences of the score generation function, not measured discriminative ability of a real verification system. The random-patch null AUROC=0.667 is similarly constructed.

CONTAMINATION_HARDCODED_NOT_MEASURED: Contamination events are explicitly set to 2 for two specific failing instances (lines 468-474) and 0 elsewhere. The reported mean 0.0046 and max 0.0833 are properties of this hardcoding, not observed system behavior.

AMORTIZATION_MATHEMATICAL_CONSEQUENCE: C8 failure (amortized tokens 4744 > cold 2226) is a direct arithmetic consequence of simulation parameters: retrieval_cost_tokens=320 (hardcoded), verification_tokens_cost=180 (hardcoded), repair_tokens_mean_test=1364 (simulated). 1364 + 180 + 10*320 = 4744 > 2226. This tests parameter choices, not real economics.

TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT_INTEGRITY_CONCERN: Verification scores are generated by deterministic_int(f"verif_score:{instance_id}", 1000) (line 500). The threshold is fit on TRAIN but the score function uses instance_id which encodes family/variant/seed. Since TRAIN/TEST split is by seed (0-2 vs 3-5), the score distributions may not be independent of the split mechanism, though the code attempts to separate them.

SUBSTRATE_SIMULATION_NOT_REAL_NGINX: Byte identity 960/960 is verified on synthetic gzip-compressed strings (simulate_byte_identity lines 125-153), not on real nginx HIT/SWR/SIE/304 responses with production Content-Encoding, chunked transfer, or Vary headers. The oracle-free decompression path is gzip.decompress on synthetic data, not the runtime's actual decompression code path.

PERTURBATIONS_SYNTHETIC_NOT_PRODUCTION: DOM perturbations are selector string changes (#submit-123->#submit-124) in simulated templates, not real accessibility tree mutations. Endpoint perturbations are query param/header name changes in simulated API dicts. Cache perturbations are Cache-Control/ETag value changes in simulated response headers. Blast radius=1 by construction in the simulation.

ORACLE_CEILING_GAP: Oracle hand-patch (B-ORACLE) achieves 100% success at 120 tokens (5.3% of cold cost), while simulated autonomous repair achieves 83% success at 1430 tokens (63.7% of cold). This 12x gap between oracle ceiling and autonomous performance in simulation suggests the heuristic is far from optimal, but does not inform real LLM capability.

POSITIVE_CONTROL_PC2_UNDERPOWERED: PC2 uses n=12 oracle patches with 11 successes (91.7%). While this passes the >=0.90 threshold, the Wilson 95% CI is [0.64, 0.99] - the lower bound is well below 0.90, making the gate pass potentially fragile.

DECISION_RULE_CORRECTLY_APPLIED: The producer correctly applied the frozen decision rule: C1-C3 PASS (measurement valid), C4 PASS, C5 FAIL, C6 PASS, C7 PASS, C8 FAIL -> overall FALSIFIES. The outcome is a valid negative per the frozen spec, not MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
baseline_findings: B-COLD-FULL-REEXPLORATION: Cold cost tokens mean 2244 (simulated), browser 8.7 (simulated), success 0.944. Baseline cost parameters are hardcoded (COLD_TOKENS_BASE=2250, COLD_BROWSER_BASE=8.2) with deterministic jitter. Not a measured baseline.
B-VERBATIM-REPLAY: Success 0.028 (1/36) - one C1 seed=0 instance hardcoded to succeed. Correctly demonstrates perturbations are breaking in simulation.
B-RETRIEVAL-RAG: Success 0.333 (12/36) - hardcoded to 30-40% range per family. Repair exceeds by 50pp. Baseline behavior is simulation parameter, not measured retrieval system.

B-ORACLE-HAND-PATCH: 100% success, 120 tokens, 1 browser interaction. Oracle ceiling is hardcoded (ORACLE_TOKENS=120, ORACLE_BROWSER=1). Provides cost ceiling reference but not achievable by simulated heuristic.
B-RUNTIME-BYTE-IDENTITY: 960/960=1.0 on synthetic gzip.decompress. Passes C3 gate but only validates simulation's own decompression logic, not runtime's actual nginx HIT-cache substrate.
PC-LOCALIZED-REPAIR-SUCCEEDS: PC1=1.0 (12/12), PC2=0.917 (11/12) token ratio 0.053. C1 gate passes but PC2 CI includes values well below 0.90.
NC-ZERO-AND-DISTANT-PERTURBATION: NC1 cost=0, cont=0; NC2 cont=0; random-patch FA=0.033, AUROC=0.667. All hardcoded/null by construction. C2 gate passes.
claim_ceiling: In a deterministic simulation with hardcoded cost parameters, a simulated heuristic repair achieves 83% pooled success (95% CI [0.68, 0.92]) at 61% of simulated cold token cost (95% CI [0.57, 0.66]) and 43% of simulated browser interactions (95% CI [0.40, 0.47]), failing the pre-registered <50%/<40% thresholds. Amortized cost at 10 reuses (4744 tokens) exceeds cold cost (2226 tokens) by 2.1x. Verification achieves AUROC=1.0 and precision=1.0 by construction of the simulation's score generation function. Contamination is hardcoded to mean 0.46% (max 8.3%). This experiment validly falsifies the cost-bounded repair hypothesis FOR THIS SIMULATION but does not test C-DELTA-REPAIR for real LLM agents because no real LLM, browser, or verification system was measured.

Whether real verification on actual DOM/response state achieves AUROC >=0.75 and precision >=0.80 without perfect-separation artifacts
Whether contamination remains <10% when measured on real registry/mechanism state rather than hardcoded events
Whether the 12x gap between oracle ceiling (5% of cold) and simulated autonomous repair (64% of cold) narrows with a real LLM
Whether per-family cost heterogeneity exists at adequate sample sizes (current TEST n=6 per family is exploratory)
Whether amortization economics change with real retrieval costs (currently hardcoded 320 tokens) and real verification costs
Whether the nginx HIT/SWR/SIE/304 byte identity holds on real infrastructure with production traffic patterns
Whether multi-resource perturbations (radius 2-3) or cross-page drift exhibit different repair cost profiles
